page.title: What can I ask?
page.intro: Before you sign a commercial lease, you need to know two things: what you can ask to change, and what can cost you the most. This tool finds key clauses in a lease and shows them three ways. Look at each one.
page.youMeans: In these explanations, "you" means the tenant: the business renting the space.
page.governs: An AI wrote these explanations to help you read the lease. Check each one against the lease text. The lease text governs.
page.glossaryHint: Tap an underlined word to see what it means.
page.nextStepsIntro: Here is every ask on this page in one list. Before you sign, send it to the landlord in writing, and keep a copy.
page.footer: Prototype for a Northeastern University School of Law class. Not legal advice.
page.uploadIntro: Upload a commercial lease as a PDF. The tool finds the key clauses and shows them three ways. It works with the Greater Boston Real Estate Board standard form, or a lease that uses the same wording.

negotiable.label: Ask before you sign
negotiable.askIntro: Before you sign, ask the landlord in writing for:

consequence.scale: Ranked from 1, the clause that can cost you the most.

glossary.meaning: The landlord: the owner who rents the space to you.
You, the tenant: the business renting the space.
The space you are renting.
Money you owe on top of your base rent. The lease counts it as rent.
The landlord's costs of running and keeping up the building and its land. This section lists what counts.
Money spent on a lasting improvement to the building, such as a new boiler or roof.
Spread out over several years. You pay a yearly share, not the whole cost at once.
Hand your lease over to another business, which takes your place as tenant.
Rent some or all of your space to another business while you stay the tenant.
Permission in writing, which you must get before you act.
Even so. Here: even if the landlord says yes.
Legally responsible. If someone else doesn't pay, you must.
Promises you make in the lease.
Failing to do something the lease requires, such as paying rent on time.
A written message from the landlord about a problem. Your time to fix it starts from the notice. Section 20 says when a notice counts as delivered, which can be when it is mailed.
Unable to pay your debts as they come due.
Handing your business property to someone who sells it to pay the people you owe.
Come back into the space and take it back from you.
Your belongings in the space, such as furniture, equipment and stock.
Without giving up any of the landlord's other ways to get paid.
Money that is overdue.
Pay someone back for a loss. Here, you pay the landlord back for the rent it loses.
The time left on the lease.

clauses.heading: 6B. Operating Cost Escalation
clauses.legalTextNote: Paste two or three sentences from your copy of sec. 6B. Do not paste the whole section.
clauses.findStart: The LESSEE shall pay to the LESSOR as additional rent
plain: You must pay a set percentage of any increase in the building's operating costs above the base year. You pay this on top of your base rent.
Operating costs include insurance, repairs, snow removal, staff pay, and some building improvements.
The lease sets no limit on how much this amount can rise.
clauses.cardLine: Your rent can rise when building costs rise.

clauses.heading: 13. Assignment - Subleasing
clauses.legalTextNote: Paste two or three sentences from your copy of sec. 13. Do not paste the whole section.
clauses.findStart: The LESSEE shall not assign or sublet
clauses.findEnd: covenants and conditions of this lease.
plain: You must get the landlord's written consent before you sublet the space or transfer the lease to someone else.
The lease does not say the landlord needs a reason to refuse.
If the landlord consents, you must still pay all the rent and keep every other promise in the lease.
clauses.cardLine: If you sublet, you still owe all the rent.

clauses.heading: 19. Default and Bankruptcy
clauses.legalTextNote: Paste two or three sentences from your copy of sec. 19. Do not paste the whole section.
clauses.findStart: The LESSEE shall default in the payment of any installment of rent
clauses.findEnd: during the residue of the term.
plain: When this applies: you have not paid rent 10 days after the landlord gives you written notice, or you have not fixed another broken promise in the lease 30 days after written notice.
What the landlord may do: end the lease, take back the space, and remove your belongings.
What you must still pay: the rent the landlord loses for the rest of the lease term, and the landlord's cost of fixing the problem, including lawyer's fees, plus interest.
This section also covers bankruptcy. Read sec. 19 for those terms.
clauses.cardLine: Late rent can cost you the space, and you still owe the rent.
